note: D-A11Y-1's deferral rests on a MEASUREMENT, and a measurement has a platform. This file records that platform so the deferral cannot outlive its own evidence.
premise: No window Quickshell creates publishes an AT-SPI tree, so nothing the guide declares reaches a screen reader.
upstream: quickshell#1144 (OUR report, closed 2026-09-21 with no comment). Cause confirmed and FIXED upstream at quickshell-mirror/quickshell@916a0dd, authored 2026-08-28: 'launch: avoid creating multiple QApplications -- Accessibility hooks created by QQuick module init are destroyed by the QApplication destructor and not recreated by a new QApplication.' NOT RELEASED: latest release v0.3.1 was published 2026-08-21, a week before the fix. Verified against the GitHub API 2026-09-25; see docs/ACCESSIBILITY-INVESTIGATION.md section 10.
whyItMatters: D-A11Y-1 is deferred under ruling AX2, which REFUSED masking the accessible Value of the Sources form fields on the grounds that live risk is zero while nothing is published at all. That is true and it is CONDITIONAL. The moment a Quickshell or Qt update makes a PanelWindow publish, the deferral stops being free: a revealed playlist or EPG URL, and the never-maskable Xtream server and username, publish their credentials to any listener on the session bus. Nothing would have noticed. The premise was a comment in three files and an assertion in none, which is the exact shape CLAUDE.md rule 13 is about -- two things joined by a NAME, where nothing verifies the join.
notADetector: This does NOT detect that the fix is installed. It detects that the EVIDENCE HAS EXPIRED, which is the honest and cheap thing to detect. A version change is the event after which the measurement no longer describes this machine, so it is the right moment to re-measure rather than to keep deferring. What to look for when it fires is in `upstream`: the first quickshell release after v0.3.1 that contains 916a0dd.
onRed: FIRST check whether the new quickshell contains 916a0dd (its changelog, or `git log --oneline v0.3.1..<tag> -- src/launch` on the mirror). If it does, assume the tree now publishes and treat D-A11Y-1 as LIVE until measured otherwise. THEN re-run scripts/a11y-probe.sh (it needs a graphical session and its baseline is deliberately red -- compare against docs/QA-A11Y.md). If a PanelWindow now publishes, D-A11Y-1 is LIVE and the field values must be masked before anything ships. If it still publishes nothing, update the versions below and say where it was re-measured.

evidence.upstreamFix: Checked per onRed on 2026-10-31, after the system update installed the three versions above: the installed quickshell, 0.3.2.r7.g2b4501a-1 (a build seven commits past v0.3.2), contains 916a0dd. So the premise is assumed broken and D-A11Y-1 is treated as LIVE until measured otherwise.
evidence.probe: scripts/a11y-probe.sh re-run on 2026-10-31 on this platform, under the nested headless cage on a private D-Bus: 84 checks, 7 failures, OFF BASELINE. The three recorded baseline failures stand -- L2-XT-05 and L2-XT-06 (the Xtream server and username published on text/text, which is D-A11Y-1 at the sink) and L2-XT-11 -- and four are new: L2-Q-04-LIT, L2-Q-06, L2-SC-03-LIT and L2-SC-06. The probe hosts the guide in a plain Window rather than a PanelWindow, so it shows what the guide publishes once its window publishes, not whether a Quickshell PanelWindow now does.

exception.why: The product owner decided on 2026-10-31 that D-A11Y-1 stays open and is fixed separately, and that meanwhile this narrow, dated exception lets work unrelated to it land on dev. NOTHING SHIPS while it stands: scripts/release.py build refuses to cut. It covers exactly the platform above and only while D-A11Y-1's board row reads open; when the fix lands the exception is removed and the premise re-measured per onRed.
